name: Six-Star Wanted System
short_description: The wanted level returns to a six-star maximum, up from GTA V's five, with escalating police response at each star.
long_description: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson confirmed to press following the August 2026 previews that GTA VI's wanted system returns to six stars, last seen in earlier era GTA titles, replacing GTA V's five-star cap. The system was demonstrated during the Extended Look and detailed further in hands-off preview sessions Rockstar gave to outlets including IGN and GamesRadar in late August 2026.

name: Police Criminal Profile System
short_description: Police build an evolving profile of a suspect's face, clothing, vehicle and weapons instead of an instant map-wide alert.
long_description: Press previews given after the August 2026 Extended Look describe a reworked wanted system where a star level is triggered only if a crime is witnessed by an NPC, reported by a victim, or caught by a security system. Police then track what they know about a suspect, shown through HUD icons covering face, outfit, vehicle and weapon, and officers stop pursuing once that information goes stale or is invalidated, for example by changing clothes or ditching a marked car. Rob Nelson described the system in interviews with outlets including IGN following the reveal.

name: Weapon Carry Limit
alt_names: two-gun limit;concealed and long gun carry system
short_description: Characters can carry only two concealed handguns and two long guns at once, replacing the unlimited weapon wheel.
long_description: Rockstar North co-studio director Rob Nelson told press after the August 2026 previews that GTA VI drops the series' effectively unlimited weapon wheel. Each protagonist can conceal up to two handguns and carry two long guns, though typically only one long gun fits on the back at a time, with a second carried openly in hand. Rifles and shotguns generally must be carried in the open or stowed in a vehicle, and NPCs react with suspicion or fear to characters openly holding long guns. Nelson said the old system \doesn't work any longer at this resolution\" given the game's NPC behavioral detail."

name: Reworked Car Theft System
alt_names: car stealing system;slim jim;key cloner;vehicle security tiers
short_description: Parked cars are split into security tiers requiring different tools, replacing GTA V's instant hotwire.
long_description: Coverage of the August 2026 Rockstar North preview sessions describes a car theft system built around vehicle security tiers. Older cars without electronic locks can be opened with a Slim Jim tool via a short minigame, while newer cars with key fobs require a key cloner device before the engine will start. Vehicles fitted with GPS trackers may require driving at a set speed to avoid detection. Carjacking an occupied vehicle remains possible as in earlier games, now with a quick-time struggle as the driver resists. Rockstar described the changes directly to outlets during the preview event.

name: Optional Romance System
short_description: Players can choose whether Jason and Lucia's relationship develops romantically or stays strictly a criminal partnership.
long_description: Press coverage following the August 2026 previews reports that although trailers present Jason and Lucia as a couple, GTA VI treats their romance as optional. Both characters begin the story with romantic interest, but the relationship only deepens through time spent together in the open world, such as shopping, salon visits, gym sessions or joint robberies, rather than through main missions alone. Ignoring calls or texts from the other character can weaken the relationship, while spending time together can rebuild it. Rockstar's Rob Nelson said the two will always remain partners in crime regardless of the player's choices, and that romance affects narrative and roleplay options rather than gameplay stat bonuses.
